Düker.et: Formally from Low German Düker, from Middle Low German düker (“diver”, also “culvert”?). Doublet of Taucher ("diver"). The sense “culvert” may be a loan translation of Dutch duiker. At least its adoption into standard German was probably reinforced by Dutch.

s: Someone who dependably supplies large amounts of money; a cash cow.
characteristic style (of writing, painting, speaking); ductus
